extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and International Searching/Examining Authorities (patent examiners) involved in the PCT international phase
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for International Preliminary Examining Authorities and applicants on conducting international preliminary examination under the PCT and on the required content and form of the international application (particularly the description and drawings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of start of international preliminary examination when ISA = IPEA
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the International Searching Authority also acts as International Preliminary Examining Authority, the international preliminary examination may start at the same time as the international search, provided the applicant has not indicated (under Rule 53.9(b)) that the examination is to be postponed until after the time limit for filing amendments under Article 19.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examination may start simultaneously subject to possible need to invite applicant to provide copies of amendments under Article 34. If the statement concerning amendments indicates postponement, the IPEA does not start until (i) it receives Article 19 amendments, (ii) it receives a notice the applicant does not wish to make Article 19 amendments, or (iii) the time limit under Rule 46.1 for filing Article 19 amendments expires. If postponed until expiration of the time limit for making a demand (Rule 54bis.1(a)), the IPEA waits until that time unless Rule 69.1(b) applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner assignment preference
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as examination is to begin, the international application is sent to an examiner responsible for establishing the international preliminary examination report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the ISA and IPEA are part of the same national Office, the international preliminary examination should preferably be performed by the examiner who was responsible for the international search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-up search objective and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA carries out a top-up search normally at the start of the international preliminary examination process to discover relevant documents that became available after the international search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No top-up search is carried out if the Authority considers such a search would serve no useful purpose. See paragraph 19.15 for further discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to at least one written opinion on patentability criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant generally has the right to receive at least one written opinion essentially directed to whether the claimed invention is novel, involves an inventive step (is non-obvious) and is industrially applicable prior to the report being established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is excepted where the IPEA considers that all of the following are fulfilled: (i) the invention appears to satisfy Article 33(1) (novel, inventive, industrially applicable), (ii) the international application complies with the Treaty and Regulations checked by the IPEA, and (iii) the Authority does not intend to make other permitted observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of documents cited in ISR and supplementary ISR
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of the international search report and any supplementary international search report are transmitted by the International Bureau to the IPEA, and all documents cited therein are taken into consideration during the international preliminary examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IPEA also considers other documents deemed relevant. The IPEA is not obliged to draw up a written opinion on claims for which an international search report has not been established. A supplementary search report received after the Authority has begun drawing up the written opinion or examination report need not be taken into account (Rule 45bis.8(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of ISA written opinion as first written opinion of IPEA
rubrics_metrics.description: The written opinion established by the International Searching Authority under Rule 43bis.1 is usually considered to be the first written opinion of the IPEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: IPEAs may notify the IB that written opinions by specified ISAs shall not be considered for this purpose; if so, the IPEA must notify the applicant. In any case, the IPEA should take the ISA's opinion into account when establishing its own written opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Article 34 and Article 19 amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant is entitled to file amendments under Article 34, which will be taken into account for subsequent written opinions and the international preliminary examination report, as will any amendments made under Article 19, unless reversed/superseded or filing requirements not met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments are not taken into account if the applicant fails to comply with Rule 46.5(b)(iii) or Rule 66.8(a), for example failing to indicate the basis for the amendments filed in the application as originally filed. Details of permissible amendments in Chapter 20. Because a Rule 43bis.1 written opinion (when treated as the first IPEA opinion) includes a time limit for response, it is usually necessary for amendments or arguments to be filed at the same time as the demand for them to be taken into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuing further written opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a top-up search finds prior art and the IPEA intends to raise objections, a further written opinion should be issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In other cases further written opinions may be issued at the Authority's discretion provided sufficient time is available, the applicant makes an effort to meet objections, and the Authority has resources. The Authority may also communicate informally with the applicant in writing, by phone or by interview. (Rules 66.2, 66.4, 66.6)

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of the international preliminary examination report (IPRP)
rubrics_metrics.description: The report does not state whether the claimed invention is or seems to be patentable according to the law of any country; it states by 'Yes' or 'No' in relation to each claim whether such claim seems to satisfy the three criteria (novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability), each accompanied by citations and explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report is an opinion on the three PCT criteria, not a national patentability decision. (Article 35(2); Rule 70)

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for establishing the IPRP
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA must establish the international preliminary examination report within whichever of the following periods expires last: (i) 28 months from the priority date; (ii) six months from the time provided under Rule 69.1 for the start of examination; or (iii) six months from receipt by the IPEA of any translation furnished under Rule 55.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are mandatory timing constraints for issuing the IPRP. (Rules 69.2; 70.15(b))

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal of the IPRP and related documents to applicant and IB
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA transmits the international preliminary examination report to both the applicant and the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IPEA also transmits other documents in its file to the International Bureau, including any written opinion by the Authority, any amendments and letters furnished by the applicant under Article 34, and any letter submitted by the applicant under Rule 66.3. (Rule 71.1(a), 71.1(b), Section 602bis)

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential treatment of IPEA file until establishment of report
rubrics_metrics.description: Until the international preliminary examination report has been established, the file of the international preliminary examination remains confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neither the IB nor the IPEA may allow access to the file unless requested or authorized by the applicant. Once the IPRP is established, the IPEA should provide documents to any elected Office requesting them. Authorized copies may be provided to third parties at the request of the applicant or authorized person, subject to reimbursement of costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of IPRP and related documents after 30 months
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the report has been transmitted to elected Offices by the IB, 30 months from the priority date the IB will make the report and other documents available to the public on behalf of those elected Offices who have requested the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes any translation and observations made by the applicant on the translation. (Rule 94.1(c))

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal of IPRP to elected Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: The IB transmits the IPRP and documents to elected Offices after 30 months from the priority date, or earlier if the applicant requests early national processing under Article 40(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmittal by the IB to any elected Office is effected only upon request by that Office and at the time specified by that Office. (Rules 73.2, 93bis.1)

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of the IPRP into English
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the IPRP is established in a language other than English, the International Bureau translates the report into English and transmits the translation to elected Offices who requested it and to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant is entitled to make written observations on the correctness of the translation and must send copies of those observations to the IB and to each interested elected Office. (Rule 72)

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to request copies of documents cited only in IPRP
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time within seven years of the international filing date, the applicant or any elected Office may request copies of any documents cited in the IPRP which were not cited in the ISR, subject to payment of costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IPEA may send copies of such citations automatically with the IPRP to the applicant. (Article 36(4); Rule 71.2)

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory contents of the international application (other than claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application must contain: (i) a request, (ii) a description, (iii) one or more claims, (iv) one or more drawings where required, and (v) an abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This chapter discusses description and drawings insofar as they concern the ISA and IPEA. (Article 3(2))

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of disclosure (Article 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application must 'disclose the invention in a manner sufficiently clear and complete for the invention to be carried out by a person skilled in the art.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The description together with drawings must supply all technical information required to enable a skilled person to put the invention into practice and enable the reader to understand the contribution to the art. See paragraphs 5.43 to 5.53 for application to all claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended structure and subheadings of the description
rubrics_metrics.description: The description should start with the same title as the request and contain subheadings corresponding to Section 204: 'Technical Field', 'Background Art', 'Disclosure of Invention', 'Brief Description of Drawings', 'Best Mode(s) for Carrying Out the Invention', and 'Industrial Applicability'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of such subheadings is strongly recommended to provide uniformity in publication and facilitate access. Some subheadings are discussed in following paragraphs; examiner may allow departures if clearer or more economic presentation results. (Rule 5.1)

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical field indication
rubrics_metrics.description: The application should specify the technical field to which it relates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear technical field assists understanding and classification. (Rule 5.1(a)(i))

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of background art
rubrics_metrics.description: The description should mention any background art of which the applicant is aware and which is useful for understanding the invention and its relationship to the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification of documents reflecting such art, especially patent specifications, should preferably be included. See appendix to chapter for further guidance. (Rules 5.1(a)(ii), 6.3(b)(i))

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of invention (problem and solution)
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention as claimed should be disclosed so that the technical problem(s) it deals with can be appreciated and the solution can be understood; include only such details as are necessary for elucidating the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not necessary to present explicitly in problem-and-solution form. State advantageous effects compared to prior art without disparagement or misleading presentation. If in doubt whether details are necessary, the examiner should not require excision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief description of drawings requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If drawings are included they should first be briefly described (e.g., 'Figure 1 is a plan view...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When referring in the description to drawing elements, use the name of the element as well as its number (e.g., 'resistor 3 is connected to capacitor 5 via switch 4'). Description and drawings should be consistent, especially reference numbers. Examiner need not rigorously require deletion of superfluous references after amendment deletions, but all reference numbers used in description or claims should appear on drawings. (Paragraphs 4.08–4.09)

rubrics_metrics.name: Best mode disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application should set forth at least the best mode contemplated by the applicant for carrying out the invention, in terms of examples where appropriate and with reference to drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-prong inquiry: (1) subjective — did applicant contemplate a best mode at filing; (2) objective — does the written description disclose the best mode so a skilled person could practice it. Examiner should assume best mode disclosed unless inconsistent evidence. Objections on best mode are extremely rare; national practices diverge and in some States failure to describe best mode has no effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and function description balance
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention must be described not only in terms of structure but also in terms of function, unless functions of parts are immediately apparent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In some fields (e.g., computers) functional description may be more appropriate than structural details. Program listings cannot be relied on as sole disclosure; description should be in normal language possibly with flow diagrams. Short program excerpts are acceptable to illustrate an embodiment. (Paragraphs 4.11, 4.23)

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency and irreparable insufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is responsible for supplying sufficient disclosure at filing to meet Article 5 for all claims; serious insufficiency cannot be cured subsequently without offending Article 34(2)(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insufficiency can render claims too broad and fail support requirements. Two special irreparable cases: (a) dependence on chance (irreproducible results, e.g., certain microbiological processes), and (b) inherently impossible inventions contrary to physical laws (e.g., perpetual motion). (Paragraphs 4.12–4.13)

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability reference
rubrics_metrics.description: The description should address industrial applicability; see chapter 14 for discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 33(1),(4); Rule 5.1(a)(vi) noted; provide information showing applicability in some industry or practical application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing and biological deposit requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the application contains nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences (≥10 nucleotides or ≥4 amino acids), include a separate sequence listing complying with Annex C of the Administrative Instructions. If biological material is referred to and cannot otherwise be described, a deposit may be taken into consideration for sufficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to specified paragraphs for handling at search and examination stages. Deposits are considered part of the description to the extent needed for sufficiency; mere reference to deposit may not suffice. In some Authorities, deposit also considered for support under Article 6. Sheets referring to deposits must be in same language as description to obtain filing date; otherwise ISA may notify RO that application should be considered withdrawn. (Rules 5.2; 13bis; AI Annex C; paragraphs 4.15–4.20)

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation, clarity, terminology and units
rubrics_metrics.description: The manner and order of presentation should follow Rule 5.1(b) unless a different order yields better understanding; description should be clear, straightforward, and avoid unnecessary technical jargon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use generally accepted technical terms, define little-known terms, maintain consistent terminology and signs. In computer field, program listings cannot be sole disclosure. Specify units when properties referred to; use metric/SI and degrees Celsius; other physical values in internationally recognized units. Use agreed international standards where practicable. (Paragraphs 4.21–4.24)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of proper names and references to other documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of proper names to refer to materials or articles is undesirable unless the word has become internationally accepted with precise meaning; references to other documents may be background art or part of disclosure and must be handled accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a referenced document is essential to satisfy Article 5 it should be incorporated into the description so the specification is self-contained. A reference to an unpublished application is not part of disclosure unless made public on or before the publication date of the international application. References to textbooks/periodicals are allowable only if content was fixed prior to filing date. (Paragraphs 4.25–4.27)

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements and discretion on drawings text
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal requirements for drawings are set out in Rules 11.10 to 11.13; only indispensible text should be on drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For complex system diagrams, identifying catchwords for functional integers may be regarded as indispensable; such items can often be identified by numerals explained in description. (Rule 11)

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited expressions and irrelevant matter (Rule 9.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are four categories of expressions prohibited in an international application: (i) matter contrary to morality or public order (e.g., incitement to riot, discriminatory propaganda, grossly obscene matter), (ii) (other categories), (iii) libelous/disparaging statements (distinguish from permitted fair comment), and (iv) obviously irrelevant or unnecessary matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 9 confines material likely to induce riot/public disorder or criminal/offensive behavior. Examiner will rarely invoke the rule. Disparaging statements are prohibited but fair comment (e.g., recognized disadvantages) is permitted. Irrelevant matter that is 'obviously irrelevant or unnecessary' should be removed; such matters may be removed by RO, ISA, Authority or IB and the applicant should be informed of the category applied. (Rule 9.1; paragraphs 4.29–4.32)

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix guidance on incorporating background art references
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorities have divergent practices on inviting applicants to introduce references to prior art into the international application; insertion of subsequently identified documents into the statement of prior art may be appropriate provided the amendment would not go beyond the disclosure as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may invite inclusion of a reference and brief summary of relevant contents, but must take care not to contravene Article 34(2)(b). The examiner should not invite insertions amounting to treatises or explanatory matter readily available in textbooks or well known in the art.
